feature_contracts.description: After synchronous reset the design shall present a deterministic safe idle state with no valid actuator update and fault reporting asserted until software clears it.
A firmware write to the control register shall be accepted through the MMIO interface and reflected in the CSR read data path.
The request packer shall drive request valid/data outputs without requiring request-ready as an output, and request-ready remains an input-controlled handshake condition.
The response unpacker shall consume response valid/data inputs and drive response ready as an output.
A faulted or malformed response path shall inhibit actuator validity and assert safe mode.
When an authorized response is accepted, the actuator command shall remain bounded by the programmed min and max limits.
A firmware fault-clear write shall be decoded through the CSR path and influence the latched fault state under top-level supervision.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level controller that owns the firmware register window, request packer, response unpacker, safety supervisor, actuator clamp/rate-limit logic, and optional small history capture backed by technology-neutral block RAM. The top emits compact model requests, accepts compact model responses, supervises link health, and only authorizes actuator updates when enable, handshake, sequence, freshness, and fault conditions are all satisfied.
top_module.functionality: Implements the complete external-service transport and safety contract. The top-level register bank provides enable, mode select, safe-position command, min/max actuator limits, rate-limit setting, timeout threshold, stale-data threshold, sequence counters, last-seen timestamp, fault status, fault clear, and link health indicators. The request packer assembles a 128-bit request packet from configuration, flow-condition metadata, geometry-handle metadata, sequence number, and timestamp, with geometry referenced only by handle/ID. The response unpacker decodes a 128-bit response packet into command recommendation, status flags, sequence echo, timestamp echo, and validity bits. The safety supervisor authorizes actuator updates only when global enable is asserted, request/response handshake is complete, response valid is high, sequence echo matches expected sequence, response age is within timeout, and no fault bits are present. Stale-data detection uses a free-running counter/timestamp compare and detects sequence gaps/replays. Actuator clamping enforces programmed min/max bounds and optional rate limiting. On any invalid, missing, stale, malformed, or faulted packet, the design inhibits actuator validity, asserts fault reporting, and latches fault status for software handling; it does not silently substitute a command.
responsibilities: Expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with decode, readback, write strobes, ready/accept semantics, and register-defined status visibility.
Pack compact model-request packets and unpack compact model-response packets without implementing the surrogate model.
Maintain bounded actuator command generation with min/max clamp and rate-limit enforcement.
Supervise link health, sequence tracking, timeout, stale-data, and malformed packet detection.
Provide deterministic reset state and deterministic fault-latched software handling.
Optionally capture recent compact packets in technology-neutral block RAM for debug/history without flattening into registers.
top_module.reset_behavior: On synchronous reset deassertion/entry through rst_n low, all outputs are driven to deterministic safe values: cfg_ready low, req_valid low, req_data zeroed, rsp_ready low or quiescent per internal link state, actuator_cmd held at the programmed safe-position value after configuration reset defaults, actuator_valid low, actuator_fault asserted until cleared by software, and safe_mode asserted. Sequence counters, last-seen timestamp, link-health indicators, and fault latches reset to known values. No fallback command substitution is performed during reset; output validity is simply deasserted and faults are latched for software handling.
behavior_rules: The top-level CSR/MMIO window must decode all implemented registers and fields described in register_contract; no declared register may be inaccessible.
The request packer must include configuration-derived mode bits, flow metadata, geometry handle/ID, sequence number, and timestamp in the 128-bit request payload.
The response unpacker must extract command recommendation, validity, status flags, sequence echo, and timestamp echo from the 128-bit response payload.
req_valid and req_data are outputs; req_ready is an input. rsp_valid and rsp_data are inputs; rsp_ready is an output.
A model request is considered launched only when req_valid and req_ready are both asserted in the same cycle.
A model response is considered accepted only when rsp_valid and rsp_ready are both asserted in the same cycle.

Actuator authorization requires enabled control plane, accepted request/response transaction completion, valid response payload, sequence echo match, age/timeout check pass, no stale-data condition, and no fault bits.

Sequence gaps, replayed sequence echoes, invalid validity bits, malformed status encodings, timeout expiry, or stale-data thresholds cause actuator_valid to deassert, actuator_fault to assert, and safe_mode to assert.
Actuator command outputs are clamped to programmed minimum and maximum bounds and optionally rate-limited against the previous accepted command within the programmed delta per update.
The design may maintain compact history entries in the technology-neutral memory macro, but no large inferred memories are permitted for payload storage.
No GPU-specific logic, no floating-point compute, and no direct neural-network inference are permitted in RTL.
The top-level outputs must be driven by real RTL logic, never by child inputs only.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
modules.description: CSR/MMIO register block that implements all firmware-visible configuration and status registers. It presents decoded semantic control fields to the rest of the top-level logic and returns register read data to the top-level MMIO interface.
modules.functionality: Implements the full firmware-visible register window. Written registers include enable, mode select, safe-position command, min/max bounds, rate limit, timeout threshold, stale-data threshold, sequence base, expected sequence, geometry handle, and flow metadata. Readable registers return configuration, current status, fault status, and link-health indicators. The block does not hide inaccessible internal state as software-visible; every declared register is decoded and reachable.
responsibilities: Decode all documented MMIO addresses.
Latch writable configuration fields.
Provide readback data and ready/accept semantics.
Expose status, fault, and link-health registers to software.
Support fault clear strobe semantics.
Keep sequence/counter-related software-visible state reachable through decode.
modules.reset_behavior: All writable registers reset to deterministic defaults: enable low, mode select zero, safe-position set to a defined safe code, min/max bounds to safe defaults, rate-limit disabled or zero, timeout and stale thresholds to conservative defaults, sequence base and expected sequence reset, last-seen timestamp reset, and fault-clear deasserted. Readback returns these defaults after reset until written. Fault and link-health status are reported through input-fed status fields from the top-level supervisor.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
Status fields are software-visible through readback and/or status inputs captured by the top-level.
No internal state may be mislabeled as software-visible unless it is decoded here.
This block is the sole producer of semantic configuration fields used by other modules.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_req_packer
modules.description: Composes the 128-bit external model request packet from semantic configuration, flow metadata, geometry-handle metadata, sequence number, timestamp, and link status. The geometry itself is not transported; only a compact handle or ID is included.
modules.functionality: Builds the outbound request packet and presents it on the external transport. The packet fields are compact and architecture-neutral, carrying only semantic metadata and sequence/timestamp information needed by the surrogate service.
responsibilities: Assemble 128-bit request payload fields.
Emit req_valid and req_data as outputs, obeying the transport direction contract.
Use geometry handle/ID only; never emit raw vehicle geometry or large tensors.
Provide sequence and timestamp echoes for downstream tracking.
Mark request launch events when the handshake completes.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, request outputs are cleared and no packet launch occurs. Sequence and timestamp outputs are zeroed or held to defined reset values until configuration becomes valid.
behavior_rules: req_valid is asserted only when the request packet is well-formed and the control plane permits transmission.
The packet must remain stable while req_valid is high and req_ready is low.
No surrogate model computation is performed here.
Geometry is transported only as a compact handle or ID.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_rsp_unpacker
modules.description: Decodes the 128-bit external model response packet into command recommendation, status flags, validity bits, sequence echo, and timestamp echo. It also reports response freshness and malformed packet indications to the safety supervisor.
modules.functionality: Unpacks the external response packet into a compact command recommendation and associated status/echo fields. The block performs only transport decoding and validity extraction; it does not compute aerodynamics or emulate the surrogate service.
responsibilities: Decode response payload fields.
Provide response validity and malformed indications.
Capture sequence echo and timestamp echo for the safety supervisor.
Drive rsp_ready as the output-side ready signal per the transport contract.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, response-derived outputs are cleared and rsp_ready is driven to a quiescent value until the top-level can accept traffic.
behavior_rules: Response decode must be synchronous and registered for timing closure.
Malformed encodings or invalid validity bits must be reported to the safety supervisor.
The decoder never substitutes or transforms the recommended command into a fallback command; it only reports what was received.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety_supervisor
modules.description: Sequence, timeout, stale-data, fault, and authorization supervisor that decides whether actuator updates may be applied. It gates valid updates only when enable, handshake completion, response validity, sequence echo, freshness, and fault conditions all satisfy the contract.
modules.functionality: Evaluates the authorization contract for actuator updates. It checks global enable, request/response handshake completion, response validity, sequence echo match, response age against timeout, stale-data threshold, sequence gaps/replays, malformed packets, and fault bits. It clamps and rate-limits the candidate command only when authorized. Otherwise it inhibits valid updates, asserts fault reporting, and asserts safe mode without silently substituting a different command.
responsibilities: Authorize or inhibit actuator updates based on the full safety contract.
Enforce min/max clamp and programmable rate limiting on accepted command recommendations.
Detect timeout, stale-data, sequence mismatch, replay, and malformed response conditions.
Latch fault status for software handling.
Drive link-health indicators for firmware visibility.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, actuator_valid is deasserted, actuator_fault is asserted or held latched until software clear, safe_mode is asserted, and the supervisory errors are cleared to known states. The module does not emit a fallback substitute command; it simply inhibits validity when not authorized.
behavior_rules: Authorized actuator updates require enable, completed request/response handshake, valid response, exact or policy-allowed sequence echo, freshness within timeout/stale thresholds, and no fault bits.
Sequence gaps, replays, or echo mismatches assert seq_error and prevent valid updates.
Timeout or stale-data expiry asserts safe_mode and inhibits actuator_valid.
Rate limiting is applied only to accepted updates and only within the programmed delta per update.
No silent command replacement is allowed on invalid or faulted conditions.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_history_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral memory wrapper for compact request/response history or debug capture. It is intended to map to native block RAM in FPGA implementation and must not be flattened into registers.
modules.functionality: Provides a small bounded history store for recent compact packets or state snapshots. The wrapper exists only as a technology-neutral memory abstraction and must be inferred or mapped to block RAM through the specified memory macro contract.
responsibilities: Expose a simple synchronous RAM-style interface.
Support compact history capture without large register flattening.
Deliver readback data to the top-level supervisor or debug logic.
modules.reset_behavior: Memory output is quiescent after reset; stored contents may be undefined unless explicitly written, but the interface behavior remains synchronous and synthesizable.
behavior_rules: This module is a wrapper only; the authoritative implementation contract is the memory macro named in memory_macros.
No alternate behavioral memory model identity may be created in RTL.
The memory dout must be consumed by real RTL logic or exposed through a top-level output; it may not be left dangling.
